inputs: the user's request to start a project
1.evidence: the T1 message in the conversation only
1.rung_why: Fixed text with no choice in it; nothing for code to compute.

2.evidence: none until T3 shows the title and its directory form
2.rung_why: The model decides which part of a reply is the title, and T3 then needs the sanitized form before any helper has computed it (D3).

unsaid.decision: Which part of the user's reply is the project title, and what its directory name is
unsaid.goes_wrong: A first reply may carry the title with an assay or a path; the model decides what the title is, and T3 shows a sanitized directory name that only create (step 6) computes, so the model sanitizes it itself, which Definitions forbid
unsaid.why_rank: A wrong title is awkward to undo but changes no data, and T3b shows the real directory before any data is linked
unsaid.fix: assays takes the title and returns create's sanitized form, so T3 renders code's answer

inputs: the user's earlier phrase naming an assay
3.evidence: the T3 message; `assays` JSON in the transcript
3.rung_why: The menu is code's, but the 'Your request matches NN' line asks the model to resolve a phrase with no rule (Definitions forbid exactly that); normalisation in code already does it.

unsaid.decision: Which menu entry the user's earlier phrase matches ('Your request matches 01')
unsaid.goes_wrong: Definitions forbid resolving a phrase yourself, yet step 3 asks the model to say which entry the request matches; 'RNA-seq' could be bulk or single-cell, the user tends to confirm a suggestion with one word, and a wrong suggestion creates the wrong assay's directories and config
unsaid.why_rank: A wrong assay runs the wrong pipeline on the data; T3b names the assay, but only a user who reads it carefully catches the slip
unsaid.fix: `assays --select` on the original phrase returns the match or the ambiguity; the model only renders it

3.note: Exit 3 (assay map missing) has no branch here or at step 4 (D2).

inputs: the user's reply, passed through unchanged
4.rung_why: Resolution of the reply is code's; the model only quotes it.

5.rung_why: A written branch on an exit code; nothing to decide.

6.evidence: the project stamp, `_config/` and `raw/` directories on disk
6.rung_why: Pure code once the IDs are passed.
6.note: Exit 3 (title sanitizes to nothing, map or stamp missing) has no branch (the pilot's create exit 3).

7.rung_why: The helper names the template; the model sends it.

8.rung_why: A fixed template; the order of assays is create's list.

9.evidence: `inspect` JSON in the transcript; nothing on disk
9.rung_why: The scan is code's, but the guard runs it for an agent only on a source a human declared public, and no contract says what to do when it refuses.

unsaid.decision: What to do when the guard refuses inspect or link because no human declared the source public
unsaid.goes_wrong: An agent may run inspect, link and finalize only on a folder listed in data_sources.tsv; no contract mentions that file, so the reply to the refusal is the model's own: ask the user to run the step, ask them to declare the folder, or stop
unsaid.why_rank: Stage 00 cannot finish in a guarded session without the human's declaration and the contract offers no compliant road; the refusal itself is loud
unsaid.fix: Definitions name data_sources.tsv; a branch sends a template asking the human to declare the folder or run the step

inputs: the user's description of their file names
10.rung_why: Scope forbids composing a pattern while the step asks for 'their answer as a regex': the rule contradicts itself, and the guard refuses every named-group pattern (D4).

unsaid.decision: Turning the user's description of their file names into a sample-ID regex
unsaid.goes_wrong: Users answer in words ('the sample is the part before _R1'), so the model writes the regex; a wrong one merges or splits samples. In a guarded session the command is refused anyway (a quoted < or >), so the model then improvises a road around it
unsaid.why_rank: Sample identity feeds every later step, but T4a lists the derived IDs for confirmation and the stage's human check asks the same
unsaid.fix: The helper proposes candidate patterns from the unmatched names as a closed menu, the user picks one, T4a confirms the IDs, and the guard admits the chosen pattern by its menu number

10.note: The re-run is a branch action of step 9's inspect. A malformed pattern crashes inspect with a traceback, exit 1 and no JSON, which no step handles (D22).

11.rung_why: The human confirms the derived IDs before anything is written.
11.note: T4a's read-1 and read-2 counts are not in inspect's JSON (pilot defect); the model would have to count files itself, which Scope forbids.

12.rung_why: Link is code, but whether the reply is a yes has no rule and the link cannot be undone inside the stage.

unsaid.decision: Whether the user's reply to T4a is a yes before link runs
unsaid.goes_wrong: T4a asks to 'Confirm ... or provide a different path' with no fixed answer; 'looks fine, but what about the undetermined files?' is the model's to read, and link cannot be undone inside the stage (re-linking needs --force, which is forbidden)
unsaid.why_rank: Wrong files stay linked until the user deletes the project, but T4b and the human check show what was linked
unsaid.fix: A fixed answer (`link`), re-asked on anything else

12.note: Exit 2 (pilot) and exit 3 (D1) have no branch.

13.rung_why: A fixed template on code's count.

inputs: which assays are linked or skipped
14.rung_why: The loop is written, but what a `skip` leaves behind is not.

unsaid.decision: What happens to an assay after the user replies `skip`
unsaid.goes_wrong: T5 offers skip, but nothing removes the skipped assay: its raw/ stays empty and finalize fails on it ('raw/ is empty'), leaving a half-made project the contract tells the agent not to delete
unsaid.why_rank: A loud failure, but a dead end the user did not choose
unsaid.fix: A helper drops the skipped assay's empty directory, or finalize ignores an assay marked skipped

inputs: a data class, a purpose and an agreement reference no step collects
15.rung_why: Finalize is code, but its --data-class and --purpose arguments come from nowhere in the dialogue; the model picks them and they lock.

unsaid.decision: The dataset's data class and purpose, passed to finalize
unsaid.goes_wrong: Step 15's command carries --data-class and --purpose, but T1 promises to collect only the title, the assays and the paths, and no step asks. The model picks both, finalize locks them in dataset.tsv, and T6 never shows them. The guard lets an agent register 'public' only for a source a human declared public, so the class is fenced; the purpose (fixture, internal, pilot, commercial) is not, and it decides where the project's jobs may run: each class permits a list of venue and purpose pairs (data_policy.tsv, permitted_backends) and the local machine accepts only 'fixture' (venue_policy.py:56-87); retention follows the class, not the purpose
unsaid.why_rank: A permanent, machine-enforced record of how the data may be used, chosen without asking and never shown back
unsaid.fix: A step asks class and purpose from a closed menu built from the data policy table, T6 shows them, and finalize's refusals get a branch

15.note: Exit 2 (class, purpose, agreement or lock refusals) has no branch (pilot). The --sample-id-pattern this step repeats is refused by the guard (D4).

16.rung_why: A written branch; T9's columns need the model to split failure strings (D19).

17.evidence: T6; the stage's human check follows
17.rung_why: A fixed hand-off on code's numbers.
